previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, morbid obesity, diabetes, and recent necrotizing fasciitis of the left lower extremity was admitted from an extended care facility after developing acute shortness of breath, chest pain, and hypoxia following a shower. He was transferred on empiric heparin for suspected pulmonary embolism after an indeterminate CT at an outside hospital. Upon arrival, he was stable and asymptomatic. A repeat CT angiogram confirmed scattered nonocclusive pulmonary emboli in the left lower lobe without right heart strain. He remained on intravenous heparin and was started on warfarin, which was titrated to 7.5 mg daily as his INR rose toward the therapeutic range. The surgical team evaluated his left leg wound with vacuum dressing and recommended continuation of wound care. He was discharged to the rehabilitation facility on continued IV heparin and warfarin with plans for hematologic and surgical follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient was seen in the acute care clinic and found to have 
increasing redness and drainage from the left leg wound. His 
white blood cell count was elevated to 11.   A wound culture was 
obtained at this time and the patient was started on vancomycin 
and zosyn. The infectious disease service was consulted and they 
recommended antibiotic coverage for an additional ___ hours 
with daily dressing changes. The intravenous antibiotics were 
discontinued on ___.  

The patient's vital signs have stabilized.  He has been afebrile 
and his white blood cell count has decreased to 7.4.  The gram 
stain of his left lower leg showed PMN's, no micro-organisms.  

The patient has been unable to transition to coumadin for 
treatment of PE.  Because of this, he has been maintained on a 
heparin drip at ___ units with a goal PTT of 70-90.  He has 
been started on daily coumadin at 32mg.  He was increased to 
37.5 on ___.  His last INR has been reported at 1.2.  
Consideration was given into placement of an IVC filter.  
Venogram of lower extremities done prior to discharge and no 
blood clots visualized.  Decision made to discharge on heparin 
infusion.

The patient was discharged to the rehabilitation facility on HD 
#6 in stable condition on a heparin drip. No antibiotics were 
recommended.  He has appoinments made with the acute care 
service, hematology, and a pending appointment with Infectious 
disease.
